---
title: "Data safety and downloading outputs"
---

You now know how to work with data, notebooks, and R inside DNAnexus.

Before using the same workflow with real MCPS data, there is one rule that must be completely clear:

::: {.callout-warning title="Never download individual-level MCPS research data"}
**Individual-level MCPS research data must remain within the approved DNAnexus environment.**

Do not download individual-level MCPS data to your laptop, desktop computer, personal storage, or another device.
:::

## 1. Training data and real MCPS data are different

The exercises in this tutorial use:

```text
mcps-dnanexus-onboarding/data/example_data.csv
```

This is a **synthetic training dataset** created specifically for the tutorial.

It does not contain information from MCPS participants.

If you are completing the tutorial from a real MCPS research project, the project may also contain real research data, usually under:

```text
Data/
```

You do **not** need to open, copy, move, or download those data to complete this tutorial.

## 2. Keep individual-level data inside DNAnexus

When you begin working with real MCPS data, carry out your individual-level analyses within the approved DNAnexus environment.

For example:

```text
MCPS project data
       ↓
   JupyterLab
       ↓
       R
       ↓
individual-level analysis
```

The individual-level data remain within DNAnexus throughout this workflow.

::: {.callout-important title="Technical ability is not the same as permission"}
The DNAnexus interface may show options such as **Download** for some files.

The presence of a Download button does **not** mean that individual-level MCPS research data may be downloaded.

Always follow the MCPS data-access requirements.
:::

## 3. What about analysis outputs?

An analysis can produce many different types of output, including:

- tables;
- model estimates;
- summary statistics;
- figures;
- reports; and
- standalone files created by R.

Some outputs may be suitable to take outside DNAnexus, while others may still contain individual-level or potentially disclosive information.

The important question is therefore not simply:

> "Is this an output?"

but:

> **"Is this output safe and appropriate to export?"**

::: {.callout-caution title="Check before downloading"}
Only download analytical outputs that have been identified as safe and appropriate to export.

If you are unsure whether an output can leave DNAnexus, **do not download it until you have checked**.
:::

## 4. Your `[DX]` notebook may contain data too

A `[DX]` notebook can preserve:

- printed data;
- tables;
- model output;
- figures; and
- other results displayed inside notebook cells.

This is useful for keeping a persistent analysis record, but it also means that a notebook may contain information derived from individual-level research data.

Treat notebooks used with real MCPS data as part of the controlled research environment.

::: {.callout-warning title="Do not download research notebooks by default"}
Do not assume that a notebook is safe to download simply because it is an `.ipynb` file.

A notebook can contain displayed individual-level data or other potentially disclosive outputs.
:::

## 5. Be careful when displaying individual-level data

Functions such as:

```r
head(dat)
```

are convenient in this synthetic tutorial.

With real research data, however, displayed rows can become part of the saved notebook output.

Before displaying individual-level data, consider whether you actually need to show those rows in the notebook.

For real analyses, prefer outputs that are appropriate for the analytical task and avoid displaying unnecessary individual-level information.

## 6. Downloading an approved output

When an output has been confirmed as safe and appropriate to export, DNAnexus provides ways to download project files through its graphical interface.

The exact method you use will depend on where the approved output has been saved.

For this introductory tutorial, you do not need to download any file.

Later reference material will also show how more experienced R users can save standalone outputs from the temporary JupyterLab environment back into the persistent DNAnexus project.

## 7. A simple rule to remember

When working with real MCPS research data:

```text
Individual-level research data
            ↓
       KEEP IN DNAnexus

Analytical output
            ↓
      Is it safe and
    appropriate to export?
        /           \
      NO             YES
      ↓               ↓
Keep in DNAnexus   Export only
                   as permitted
```

If there is any uncertainty, keep the file inside DNAnexus and check before exporting it.

## Checkpoint

Before moving on, make sure you understand that:

- the data used in this tutorial are synthetic;
- individual-level MCPS research data must remain in DNAnexus;
- seeing a **Download** option does not mean a file is permitted to leave DNAnexus;
- notebooks themselves can contain individual-level or disclosive information; and
- analytical outputs should only be downloaded when they are safe and appropriate to export.

::: {.callout-success title="Core workflow complete"}
You now know how to start JupyterLab, work in a persistent `[DX]` notebook, access project data, save your work, end and restart a session, and work safely within the DNAnexus environment.

The final page provides a **quick reference and troubleshooting guide** that you can return to whenever you need it.
